value: germination in the dark was 0.4% against 40% in light; the paper's Methods contradict this: they say no germination was recorded in foil-wrapped dishes. The authors conclude from the dark result that both Ambrosia species require light for germination
method: germination in Petri dishes in light against dishes wrapped in aluminium foil to exclude light
conditions: laboratory growth chamber, 25/18 C with a 16 h day/8 h night cycle; 9 cm dishes on two layers of filter paper moistened with 500 microlitres tap water and sealed with Parafilm; seeds collected from various open-field areas 2009 to 2014 and kept dry in paper bags at 4 C; experiments repeated at least twice with five to six replications, results combined as 10 to 12 replications; the paper's Tukey Kramer HSD (P <= 0.05) is not reported for light against dark and no error measure is given for the dark value. Methods say 'No germination in Petri dishes wrapped with aluminum foil to prevent light penetration was recorded', hence all other experiments were in light; Results give 0.4% for A. confertiflora and 22% for A. artemisiifolia in the dark and 40% and 56% in light; the paper does not reconcile the two. The abstract states all three species (A. confertiflora, A. artemisiifolia, A. tenuifolia) germinate best in light from the soil surface with no stratification requirement. The quoted sentence names both A. confertiflora and A. artemisiifolia; this record takes only the A. confertiflora figure (the A. artemisiifolia figure is on main in desk-d111)

value: seeds treated with 1 mM abscisic acid (ABA) did not germinate (0%); the Results say this held at all four temperature regimes, but the Methods describe the ABA incubation only at 25/15 C for 2 weeks, and no water-control germination is printed for that test
method: seeds of wild-collected Korean pine incubated with 1 mM ABA against a distilled-water control; germination scored as a 2 mm radicle; ABA incubation described at 25/15 C, 14/10 h, 2 weeks (Section 2.4); the four regimes 10/5 to 30/20 C belong to the dormancy-release test (Section 2.3) and are named for ABA only in Results 3.1
conditions: seeds from at least 50 trees in a mixed broad-leaved Korean pine forest, Liangshui National Nature Reserve, collected late September 2020, stored at -20 C for about one month then buried in litter and soil for about eight months to release primary dormancy; Section 2.4 describes the ABA treatment as 1 mM ABA or distilled water (control) on a sterile cotton pad wetted with distilled water in sealed containers at 25/15 C, 14 h light/10 h dark (about 200 umol photons m-2 s-1) for 2 weeks, five replicates of 200 seeds per group, and does not say how the ABA was delivered; Section 3.1 reports the 0% across all four regimes although Section 2.4 names only 25/15 C, an inconsistency in the paper that this record does not resolve. The untreated (no ABA) dormancy-release germination test in Section 2.3 (three replicates of 20 seeds on filter paper with 8 mL distilled water, about eight weeks) gave 83.33 +/- 7.64% at 25/15 C and about 15% at 10/5 C; the paper does not print the water-control germination within the ABA test itself, so that 83.33% is a separate experiment's value. No statistical test is reported for the ABA result. The study's purpose was metabolomics of the radicle and of the hypocotyl plus cotyledon after ABA exposure; the dormancy-release test also gave 66.67 +/- 10.41% at 20/10 C and 56.67 +/- 15.28% at 30/20 C; the ABA seeds were incubated 2 weeks before dissection against about eight weeks in the dormancy-release test, so the 0% is not shown over the same period as the 83.33% figure

value: seeds soaked in gibberellic acid (GA3) germinated at 13 to 80%, depending on GA3 concentration and incubation temperature; germination rose with GA3 concentration
method: seeds soaked for 24 h in GA3 solutions of 10 to 1000 mg/L and germinated at the alternating regimes 25/15 C and 30/20 C, compared with seeds soaked in distilled water (wet control) and with non-soaked seeds
conditions: seeds from 50 randomly chosen individuals of a wild-growing population near Soto del Real (Spain), collected September 2014; four replicates of 25 seeds on two sheets of filter paper, 16 h light photoperiod; Table 2 final germination (mean +/- SE) at 25/15 C and 30/20 C: wet control 4 +/- 2.00 and 7 +/- 1.66%; GA3 10 mg/L 15 and 19%, 25 mg/L 13 and 25%, 50 mg/L 35 and 32%, 100 mg/L 34 and 32%, 250 mg/L 48 and 64%, 500 mg/L 61 and 58%, 1000 mg/L 72 +/- 8.60 and 80 +/- 5.10%; the 13% (25 mg/L, 25/15 C) is below the 15% at 10 mg/L, so the rise is not monotonic at the lowest doses. Untreated (non-soaked) seeds reached 2% or less after 8 weeks at all tested temperatures. Text: GA3 was significantly (p<0.05) effective against control seeds at 30/20 C for every tested concentration but at 25/15 C only for 50 to 1000 mg/L; germination correlated positively with GA3 concentration (r2=0.764, p=0.004 at 25/15 C; r2=0.742, p=0.006 at 30/20 C); arcsine-transformed data, ANOVA and LSD at 5%. A GA3 response of a physiologically dormant weed seed, not a measure of the natural cue; cold stratification (62 to 84%) was a second effective treatment in the same paper

value: gibberellic acid (GA3) treatments did not differ significantly in germination rate, germination start date or germination energy
method: GA3 at 0, 100, 250 and 500 mg/L injected into 1% agar medium; seeds germinated in darkness (under dark conditions) at constant 20 C and 25 C, alone and combined with cold stratification
conditions: seeds collected 15 October 2020 from the Nari Basin, Ulleungdo, South Korea; four replicates of 25 seeds on 1% agar, germination monitored for three months; the GA3 test was run in the dark (Section 2.6); GA3 alone gave 27.4 +/- 3.6, 31.2 +/- 6.5, 29.9 +/- 3.9 and 17.4 +/- 1.5% at 20 C and 47.1 +/- 7.6, 41.3 +/- 9.5, 41.3 +/- 9.4 and 38.6 +/- 10.8% at 25 C for 0, 100, 250 and 500 mg/L (no letter groupings read); the paper says mean germination time differed between temperatures but its relation to hormone concentration was not consistent, so no effect of the hormone was judged; combined with cold stratification, germination was 73.6 to 85.0% at 20 C and 78.4 to 91.4% at 25 C and the paper says there was no difference in the effects of hormone concentration, while the longer the cold stratification the higher the germination; Tukey HSD p < 0.05. The paper's Table 2 note says GA3 was applied only at 25 C, which conflicts with Section 2.6 and Figure 6 reporting 20 C and 25 C. A null result for a hormone treatment on seed; the species' seeds are dormant until cold stratified or placed in darkness
